chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you commence the prayer, raise your two palms, then extend them fully, then say Takbir three times, then say: 'O Allah, You are the True King, there is no god but You, Glory be to You, I have wronged myself, so forgive my sin, for no one forgives sins except You.'

Then say Takbir twice, then say: 'Here I am and at Your service, and goodness is in Your hands, and evil is not to You, and the Guided one is the one You guide, there is no refuge from You except to You, Glory be to You, and Your tenderness, Blessed and Exalted, Glory be to You, Lord of the House.'

Then say Takbir twice, then say: 'I turned my face toward the One who created the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, upright and Muslim, and I am not of the polytheists. Indeed my prayer, my rituals, my life, and my death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds, no partner for Him, and by that I was commanded, and I am of the Muslims.'
Then seek refuge from the accursed Satan, then recite the Opening of the Book.

key_terms.فَاتِحَةَ الْكِتَابِ: The Opening of the Book (Surah Al-Fatiha)

ai.seo_question: What are the recommended supplications and actions for the opening of the prayer in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific ritual sequence for the opening of prayer, emphasizing the distinct Shia practice of raising hands multiple times alongside a structured series of Takbirs and supplications. It highlights the theological emphasis on divine sovereignty and forgiveness through the recitation of 'Allāhumma anta al-malik al-ḥaqq', reflecting the Imami tradition of integrating detailed devotional acts with Quranic recitation.
